description: Looking for 2 individuals. One with animation/graphic design experience, and another with coding expertise.
summary:
At Jezero Crater on Mars, there’s now a place to sit beside Ingenuity.

Beside Ingenuity is an interactive learning experience for learners aged 10–14. In her own imagined voice, the helicopter tells the incredible story of how she became the first aircraft to achieve powered, controlled flight on another planet, and everything that led to and followed this feat.

For the Abandoned but Not Forgotten challenge, we turned the story of an abandoned machine into an immersive experience. The illustrated questions (“Talk with me”) range in complexity and reflect the curious and all-questioning minds of a young audience. To make the experience more tactile, learners can also examine the helicopter in 3D (“Examine with me”) and learn about the parts that created Ingenuity, as well as experience her actual flight paths through a printable puzzle (“Solve with me”) and a timed map (“Fly with me”).

As we near the third anniversary of Ingenuity’s mission drawing to a close, now is the right time to pause and reflect on everything Ingenuity stood and continues to stand for: hope in dark (and cold) times, persistence in moments of doubt and wavering faith, and possibility where none was promised. To keep her alive in the minds of the next generation and to celebrate her as an emblem of the enduring human capabilities of persistence and patience, Beside Ingenuity translates the legacy of something that truly lived up to its name: Ingenuity—the art of finding a way where there is none.
details:
“Sit beside me.”

Beside Ingenuity begins by inviting visitors to take a seat beside Ingenuity at Valinor Hills, her final airfield in Jezero Crater. This is accompanied by lowering an imagined helmet visor. 

The experience unfolds in four invitations.

Sit with me: Learners can chat with Ingenuity and pick from illustrated questions about her first flight, her time on Mars, her last landing, and more. All questions are categorized into four chapters: A little hello, Learning to fly, My last flight, and Now and next.

Explore with me: Offers learners an interactive 3D model of Ingenuity, with hotspots marking the various components that made up the helicopter and the roles they played.

Solve with me: Here, we adapted a NASA/JPL map of Jezero Crater into a printable jigsaw. As learners match craters, ridges, and route lines across the pieces, they put together the landscape Ingenuity flew over and see how her routes relate to Perseverance’s path. The puzzle gives families, classrooms, space clubs, and individual enthusiasts memorabilia, as well as a way to continue exploring the story away from the screen.

Fly with me: Houses our journey map, which gives that puzzle hardware a history through the routes and key statistics of her 72 flights, shown through a bird’s-eye view of the whole route and an optional view of each individual flight route. Together, the two views show what had to work for a small helicopter to lift off in thin Martian air, and how that achievement grew into something useful to the Perseverance team.

Perhaps the most innovate part of the whole experience is the “Sit quietly” feature. It allows learners to experience the abandonment of Ingenuity and gives a moment to soak in what they learn from the whole experience. A soft background score holds the silence, leaving room to feel her stillness and to let what they have learned settle.

The whole experience is built on one creative choice: instead of reading about Ingenuity, you sit beside Ingenuity. She is not presented as discarded hardware but as a companion with a story, who speaks in the first person in a young yet clear and resolute voice to relate with the target audience. Subtle animations on her stylized form change with each question, so she feels alive and present in the conversation.

Gouache-style landscapes give Mars an inviting warmth; the background plays a role too: it is a 360-degree view learners can look around in, as if they were truly sitting on the crater floor. Even the silence is part of the design: learners can close the conversation and sit quietly beside Ingenuity, with only a soft score for company. The story also continues off the screen, through a printable jigsaw, to spark users’ imagination further.

To make the experience more accessible and personalized, we have deliberately added features like high contrast, reduced motion, a sound toggle, and kept scrolling to a minimum. We built the interactive viewer with HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Three.js. We used ChatGPT and Claude for development, ElevenLabs for Ingenuity’s voiceover, and Vizcom and ChatGPT for the 360-degree gouache-style artwork, character render, and animation.

Our aim with this project is a lucid, approachable, and unforgettable learning experience that helps young audiences remember Ingenuity as the unlikely hero she was. We want learners to leave understanding what it took to defy notions, fly in thin Martian air, and how a small experiment grew into a scout for Perseverance. More than that, we want them to feel something for her: to see that what is left behind on Mars is not junk but a story. We wanted to build something rewarding both as information and as art; something able to hold her many milestones, and to travel beyond the screen into classrooms, homes, and space clubs, for the next generation of dreamers, doers, and believers.
